slot.brief: For a sparingly soluble salt of a given dissolution equation (e.g. with 2:1 stoichiometry), relate solubility s to Ksp, then compute either s from Ksp or Ksp from s; also compare solubilities of two salts with same/different stoichiometry.

stem: The molar solubility of $\text{A}_2\text{B}$ is $3.0\times10^{-4}$ mol L$^{-1}$. For $\text{A}_2\text{B}(s)\rightleftharpoons 2\text{A}^+(aq)+\text{B}^{2-}(aq)$, the value of $K_{\text{sp}}$ is:

verdicts.working: For molar solubility s = 3.0×10⁻⁴ M, [A⁺] = 2s and [B²⁻] = s. Thus Ksp = (2s)²s = 4s³ = 1.08×10⁻¹⁰ mol³ L⁻³.

working:
$[\text{A}^+]=2s,\quad [\text{B}^{2-}]=s$ 
$K_{\text{sp}}=[\text{A}^+]^2[\text{B}^{2-}]=(2s)^2s=4s^3$ 
$K_{\text{sp}}=4(3.0\times10^{-4})^3=1.08\times10^{-10}\ \text{mol}^3\text{L}^{-3}$

Independent check: For molar solubility s = 3.0×10⁻⁴ M, [A⁺] = 2s and [B²⁻] = s. Thus Ksp = (2s)²s = 4s³ = 1.08×10⁻¹⁰ mol³ L⁻³.
